fixes.explanation: Yes, friend, it's False. They appointed the priests by their divisions and the Levites by their groups "…according to what is written in the Book of Moses." (Ezra 6:18). Darius's decree covered money and supplies (Ezra 6:8-9). The assignments came from the Book of Moses, not from the king.

Yes, friend. "…the Levites slaughtered the Passover lamb for all the exiles, for their priestly brothers, and for themselves." (Ezra 6:20). They took care of it for the exiles, the priests and themselves. The Levites are the ones the text names for the job. That's a big job on a big day.

Haggai and Zechariah are the prophets in this passage, friend, and they come in with the building (Ezra 6:14). But the Passover lamb was slaughtered by someone else. "…the Levites slaughtered the Passover lamb for all the exiles, for their priestly brothers, and for themselves." (Ezra 6:20). The Levites are the ones the text names for that job.

Yes, baker. The search starts in the archives in Babylon, but the scroll is found in the fortress of Ecbatana, in the province of Media (Ezra 6:2). The search started in one city and the scroll turned up in another. That memo is the one that mentions Cyrus's decree.

Nineveh is a famous name, baker, but it's not in this search. The scroll turns up in the fortress of Ecbatana, in the province of Media (Ezra 6:2). The search itself starts in the archives in the treasury of Babylon (Ezra 6:1). Nineveh never gets a mention in these verses, so you can cancel that road trip.

Yes, baker. The memo says the gold and silver articles of the house of God, which Nebuchadnezzar took from the temple, must be returned to the temple in Jerusalem (Ezra 6:5). They are to be deposited in the house of God. That's the order, and it names exactly what Nebuchadnezzar carried to Babylon.

That sounds like a king gathering evidence, baker, but Darius isn't asking for names. His first words to Tattenai are, "You must stay away from that place!" (Ezra 6:6). Then he says, "Leave this work on the house of God alone." (Ezra 6:7). He's telling Tattenai to back off, not asking for a list.

Yes, baker. The cost is paid in full from the royal treasury "…so that the work will not be hindered." (Ezra 6:8). The money comes out of the taxes of the provinces west of the Euphrates. The aim of the decree is plain: keep the work moving.

The elders are the ones rebuilding, baker, but they're not the ones asking in this verse. The supplies are given daily "…as requested by the priests in Jerusalem…" (Ezra 6:9). The elders do get the building costs covered (Ezra 6:8). In this verse, the priests are the ones named as requesting.

Elijah and Elisha are famous, baker, but they're not in this verse. Great pair of names, wrong job site. The text names "…Haggai the prophet and Zechariah son of Iddo." (Ezra 6:14). Those two are the prophets whose prophesying went along with the building.

That's right, baker. "All the priests and Levites had purified themselves and were ceremonially clean." (Ezra 6:20). Purified is the word the text uses for them. The same verse goes on to say the Levites slaughtered the Passover lamb.
